headline: Sales edge higher as freight costs squeeze margins
summary_short: Smurfit Westrock's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose to $8,031M (+4.1% q/q, +1.1% y/y) as Basic EPS swung to $0.17 from a $0.05 loss a year ago, even as elevated freight and input costs compressed the company's own Adjusted EBITDA margin to 14.2% from 15.3% y/y.
summary_long: Net sales of $8,031M grew modestly q/q and y/y on strong paper demand, per management. Gross profit fell 7.7% y/y as freight costs rose faster than pricing could recover, though operating profit still climbed to $309M from $251M y/y on lower impairment/restructuring ($119M vs $280M) and Combination costs ($1M vs $21M). Net income reached $89M versus a $28M loss a year ago, lifting Basic EPS to $0.17. Cash of $677M was roughly flat q/q as $765M of operating cash flow covered $465M of capex and $237M of dividends. The company declared a $0.4523/share dividend and guided Q3 Adjusted EBITDA to approximately $1.3B and full-year Adjusted EBITDA to $4.9B-$5.1B.

drivers.explanation: Management cites demand for paper remaining strong through the quarter with a generally excellent supply/demand backdrop, plus continued outperformance in the EMEA/APAC and LATAM regions.
The quarter was impacted by significantly higher input costs, particularly freight, which management says it partly mitigated through its own pricing and cost actions.
Same freight and input-cost inflation cited for the gross-profit decline drove cost of goods sold higher against a smaller revenue gain.
Impairment and restructuring costs fell to $119M from $280M y/y and Combination-related transaction costs fell to $1M from $21M, more than offsetting the freight-driven gross-margin decline.
The release does not report a separate EBIT line; this shard figure moves with operating profit's improvement from lower one-off restructuring and transaction costs.
This shard's EBITDA figure diverges from the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which actually fell to $1,140M from $1,213M y/y on the same freight-cost pressure noted for gross profit.
Tracks the operating income increase from lower restructuring and transaction costs, with interest expense roughly flat y/y ($179M vs $182M).
Followed the pretax income gain and a lower income tax expense of $40M versus $84M a year ago, per the income statement.
Tracks the net income swing to a $89M profit from a $28M loss a year ago, spread over a similarly sized weighted share count.
Tracks the same net income swing as Basic EPS; diluted and basic shares produced an identical $0.17 result this quarter.
Operating cash flow of $765M exceeded the quarter's $465M capex and $237M dividend outflows, leaving cash roughly flat versus Q1; the y/y decline reflects lower operating cash flow ($765M vs $829M).
$237M of dividends paid in the quarter outweighed the $89M of net income added to retained earnings, per the cash flow and equity statements.
Management frames the quarter as strong operationally despite freight-driven cost pressure, expecting to recover input-cost inflation through the second half of 2026 and beyond.
